subject: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@fastretail.co>, Penny Delgado <penny@fastretail.co>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options

Hi James / Penny —

Thanks again for the ongoing partnership. Ahead of FastRetail's contract renewal we ran a focused health and economics pass on Q1 usage and want to surface a few practical options so you can pick what best aligns with your peak-season risk tolerance and budget cycle. Attached: fastretail-q1-usage.csv and a scenarios workbook (redwood-term-scenarios.xlsx).

Highlights from our review:
- Token footprint: 240M tokens consumed in the last 90 days, with 65% of traffic concentrated in a daily 4-hour peak window tied to checkout personalization.
- Latency: 90th percentile steady at ~110ms on hosted API; peak spikes to ~240ms under batch surges.
- Cost baseline: current pay-as-you-go unit cost implies ~$12k/month for the steady state; large peaks are the primary driver of overage spend.

Two recommended, mutually exclusive paths:
1) Predictable commit (12 months) + 25% buffer
   - Commit: 300M tokens / year (covers current + buffer)
   - Effective unit price: 18% discount vs current list
   - Benefit: predictable spend, lower per-token cost, automatic priority routing during constrained windows

2) Add Dedicated pod for peak windows (hybrid)
   - Keep hosted for baseline, provision a Dedicated GPU pool for peak hours (can be autoscaled)
   - Benefits: consistent tail latency (90th < 130ms), reserved throughput for marketing spikes, separate billing line-item

Quick ask: which direction should we model in an updated SOW? If helpful, I can run an immediate 3-scenario cost comparison (renew w/commit, renew +50M upsell, renew + dedicated) and share a line-item PO-ready quote.

Suggested next step: 30-min sync this week to align on SLA needs for peak events and to confirm the preferred billing model. Are you available Thu 2/12 10:00am or Fri 2/13 2:00pm PT?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fastretail-q1-usage.csv, redwood-term-scenarios.xlsx

From: James Liu <james.liu@fastretail.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Penny Delgado <penny@fastretail.co>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options

Vivek —

Appreciate the concise recap. A couple of clarifying asks before we lock a time:
1) Can you breakout the incremental cost to add +50M tokens (one-time vs committed discount) and show monthly run-rate differences? We need to see how that maps to our FY budget buckets.
2) For the Dedicated option, please include the SLO language (esp. tail latency SLA and remediation credits). During last year's holiday we saw downstream timeouts and want assurance.

Also please loop in Monica from ops (monica.patel@fastretail.co) — she owns infra planning on our side. Alex, feel free to prep a quick PO cadence if we decide to commit.

If Thu 2/12 10am works for you, lock it in. Otherwise Fri 2/13 2pm is also okay.

Thanks,
James
CTO, FastRetail

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@fastretail.co>, Penny Delgado <penny@fastretail.co>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options — cost breakout

James / Penny —

Quick cost breakout (high level). I expanded the workbook and uploaded a short slide in Drive (link below). Numbers rounded for discussion:

Scenario A — Renew with 12mo commit (300M tokens/yr)
- Effective unit price: $0.000045/token
- Monthly bill (amortized): ~$11,250
- Overage rate beyond commit: $0.000065/token

Scenario B — Renew + 50M committed add (350M tokens/yr)
- Effective unit price: $0.000041/token
- Monthly bill (amortized): ~$12,083
- Net incremental spend vs current run-rate: ~$1,000–1,200/mo but with lower overage risk

Scenario C — Hybrid with Dedicated peak pod (hosted baseline unchanged)
- Dedicated: reserved pool priced as monthly node units; modeled at ~$7,500/mo for a 1-node peak pool sized to cover the 4-hour window (can be scheduled)
- Benefit: reduces tail latency, eliminates most peak-driven overage events

Notes:
- For your FY planning I recommend Scenario B if you want a minimal admin lift and predictable unit economics. Scenario C is recommended if consistent sub-150ms tail latency during peaks is a hard requirement for checkout conversion targets.
- SLA: our standard enterprise SLOs (included in the SOW) provide 99.5% availability and 90th percentile latency commitments. For tighter language we can add a tailored SLA with financial credits; I'll include proposed verbiage in the SOW draft.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/fastretail/q1-usage (see tab: "scenarios")

Can confirm Thu 2/12 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite. Alex, will you also prepare an initial SOW + PO template so we can expedite once they choose?

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@fastretail.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, James Liu <james.liu@fastretail.co>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options — ops notes

Looping in a couple of practical constraints from infra: we can support a Dedicated pod that is scheduled only for the 4-hour peak window, but need 7 days' lead time to coordinate firewall rules and network ACL reviews with our cloud provider. If we go the commit route we'll want a 30-day notice prior to the contract effective date so we can reallocate capacity.

Also attaching a short ops checklist (ops-canary-checklist.pdf) — please include in the SOW an explicit rollback plan for any canary traffic shaping changes.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Infrastructure, FastRetail

Attachment: ops-canary-checklist.pdf

From: James Liu <james.liu@fastretail.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@fastretail.co>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastRetail renewal: term & scaling options — decision

Vivek / Alex —

After reviewing the scenarios with Monica, we’d like to proceed with Scenario B: renew +50M committed tokens (350M/yr) on a 12-month term. Please:
- Send an updated SOW with the effective date of 2027-03-01 and the committed volumes/discounts called out.
- Provide a PO-ready quote (we will route through procurement).
- Add the canary rollback plan language Monica requested.

Alex — can you start the SOW and route the DocuSign link to james.liu@fastretail.co when ready? We’re targeting a signed agreement by 2027-02-25.

Thanks,
James
CTO, FastRetail

P.S. Happy to take the invite Thu 2/12 10am PT but looks like we are aligned — feel free to use the call to finalize SOW details.
